The official PMR page names Lister Storm GT. A documented 2000 Lister championship car explicitly says the Storm GT used from 2000 onward had a six-speed sequential gearbox and identifies its chassis as GTM 002; it also calls the car a 2000 Lister Storm GTM. This provides the independent bridge from PMR's abbreviated display name to the existing GTM record. FIA Form GT-008 is retained as an adjacent-variant warning because its 1999 base homologation lists a Getrag six-speed manual with synchronisers.

No reviewed exact-car source supports paddles for this late-period car. The 2000-onward specification explicitly calls the gearbox sequential and describes the push-pull lever. Manual blip is a downshift action in this data model; no upshift-blip procedure is asserted. Automatic blip is a downshift action in this data model; the reviewed real-car sources do not describe an upshift blip. Throttle lift is recorded as an upshift action in this data model; no separate downshift-lift claim is made. No downshift cut is established; the source is silent on such a function. The photographed rim is continuous across the upper section; no upper opening is visible. This is evidence for the photographed 2003-spec restoration, not every earlier Storm variant. The wheel has a button hub but no integrated readout; the visible display is mounted in the dashboard behind the rim. driver_summary: The Lister Storm GTM, which Assetto Corsa lists as GT Tornado V12. Hewland TGTA six-speed sequential on a push-pull lever rather than paddles. Upshift flat and the car cuts for you. Nothing blips the downshift, so match the revs yourself: whether this gearbox needs it is not established, and a blip costs nothing.
